Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: A notice has been posted about an optional training session happening next week.
Story: I stared at the calendar on the fridge, the date of our family gathering circled in bright red. My daughter had called last night, reminding me how much the grandkids were looking forward to baking cookies and playing board games together. I could already picture their eager faces, the warmth of their hugs, the laughter echoing through the house. But this morning at the construction site, the foreman posted a notice about an optional training session—same day as the gathering. He said it would cover new safety protocols and that those who attended would be first in line for overtime shifts. I knew how important it was to stay up-to-date, to show the crew I was committed, especially with work being unpredictable lately. My coworkers were already talking about going, and I felt the pressure to join them, not wanting to fall behind or seem less dedicated. The weight of both expectations pressed on me—my family’s hope for togetherness, my team’s trust in my reliability. I stood in the kitchen, torn, the two worlds pulling me in opposite directions, unsure which part of myself I could afford to disappoint.
